# Plan and test product accessibility

[Overview](#overview) · [Before you start](#before-you-start) · [Steps](#steps-at-a-glance)

## Overview

When designing, purchasing or materially changing a digital product or customer journey. An assessed accessibility backlog, verified improvements and a published owner for remaining barriers.

Start with the applicability facts and evidence listed in the first step. Resolve missing facts before authorizing the affected work. Completion requires the documented outcome, including tracked exceptions; starting an application or recording a task is not evidence of completion.

> This is an operational coordination guide. Confirm the applicable company facts, contracts and jurisdictions before acting. Qualified advisers own legal, tax, safety or regulatory determinations and any required professional work. The cited authorities describe their named jurisdictions or frameworks; their rules are not asserted for other countries. External actions require approval for the specific action.

> Editorial status: operational draft. Source pages checked on 2026-10-29. No case-specific legal review, professional assurance or completed execution is claimed.

## Outcomes

- An assessed accessibility backlog, verified improvements and a published owner for remaining barriers.

## Step details

<a id="step-1"></a>

### 1. Scope the users, journeys and applicable targets

agent-runnable


Identify critical tasks, platforms, assistive technologies and customer commitments. Have the responsible reviewer determine any applicable legal or contractual requirements rather than claiming one test covers every jurisdiction.

- Sources: [W3C planning and managing web accessibility](https://www.w3.org/WAI/planning-and-managing/)

<a id="step-2"></a>

### 2. Agree the accessibility evaluation plan

human · human approval required


Product, design and engineering owners choose the evaluation criteria, representative pages and human testing needs. Include keyboard, screen-reader and usability checks alongside automated tools.

- Sources: [W3C planning and managing web accessibility](https://www.w3.org/WAI/planning-and-managing/)

<a id="step-3"></a>

### 3. Run technical checks and document reproducible barriers

agent-runnable


Collect automated findings and reproducible steps, environment details and affected user journeys. Separate confirmed barriers from tool suggestions and avoid treating a clean automated scan as complete accessibility.

- Sources: [W3C planning and managing web accessibility](https://www.w3.org/WAI/planning-and-managing/)

<a id="step-4"></a>

### 4. Test with qualified people and prioritize fixes

human · human approval required


Review the product with accessibility specialists or representative users where appropriate. Assign fixes based on task impact and verify design, content and engineering changes together.

- Sources: [W3C planning and managing web accessibility](https://www.w3.org/WAI/planning-and-managing/)

<a id="step-5"></a>

### 5. Retest and maintain the accessibility record

agent-runnable


Retest critical journeys and document residual limitations and support routes. Integrate checks into release review and assign responsibility for keeping any public accessibility statement accurate.

- Verify: An assessed accessibility backlog, verified improvements and a published owner for remaining barriers.
- Sources: [W3C planning and managing web accessibility](https://www.w3.org/WAI/planning-and-managing/)
